summary.verdict_text: On the video alone (physics-only), Balloon drifting with the wind scores highest, ahead of the next explanation by 3.8 log units, but this is not called decisive: without the post-hoc data-quality exclusions (a full refit) Object on a free path (no physical model) leads instead; with a rotation noise below 0.53 deg (the data-only value is 0.68 deg) H-AC leads instead; in the model-recovery test, data made by H-AC, H-ART, H-SLOW, H-WIT were also won by H-BAL, so this data cannot tell those explanations apart.
summary.settle_title: Radar range near the end of the clip
summary.settle_text: Fitted to the video alone, every physical model at 0.35 deg puts the object at 15 nmi or more at 34 s (balloon 15 to 30, slow flier 20 to 36, distant jet 18 to 55, glare on a target 18 to 61 nmi). A radar range of 10 nmi or less (the aircrew's account), good to about 2 nmi, would rule out all four by a likelihood ratio of 10 or more. At 0.7 deg this does not hold: the balloon fits at 9.0 to 13.6 nmi. The aircrew say the radar page was taped with the FLIR; it has not been released. - Balloon or slow flier. At 0.7 deg their ranges do not overlap (9.0 to 13.6 vs 19.2 to 22.1 nmi at the end), so a radar range good to 2.6 nmi separates them both ways. At 0.35 deg only a wind measurement at about 20,000 ft helps, and only one way (it can rule out the balloon, never the slow flier, which may fly at zero air speed). - Glare or physical object. Since the rotation criterion is scored on held-out data (CP-04 fix), it no longer separates them, and the recovery test confirms it (glare-made data are often won by the balloon). A radar range or closure rate separates the glare models from the balloon one way only (the glare models' bands are wide and reach their prior bounds). - Pairs no measurement separates. The distant jet and the glare-on-a-target model are the same physics here. The free path (H-WIT) can sit at any range and speed; its discriminator bands in discriminators.md are degenerate (0 nmi) and are not used here. - Field of view. It does not change the physics-only leader with the exclusions (the balloon at both), but changes its lead over the slow flier from 3.7 to 11.3 log units and moves the balloon's end range in from 15 to 30 nmi to 9 to 14 nmi. - The exclusions. Without the data-quality exclusions the free path leads at both fields of view and the balloon is fifth (results above), so any measurement that settles the size and brightness question (an unsaturated recording) also bears on the ranking.

summary.verdict_text: On the video alone (physics-only), Balloon drifting with the wind scores highest, ahead of the next explanation by 5.9 log units, but this is not called decisive: without the post-hoc data-quality exclusions (a full refit) Sensor artifact (glare in the pod optics) on a target of any type leads instead; in the model-recovery test, data made by H-ART, H-SLOW, H-WIT were also won by H-BAL, so this data cannot tell those explanations apart.
summary.settle_title: The wind at 13,200 ft is the discriminator
summary.settle_text: A balloon's air speed is 0 to 2.7 kt; the slow flier allows 0 to 18.5 kt (best 9.6), the free path 11 to 30 kt (best 23). An independent wind good to 3.9 kt separates the balloon from the free path both ways (ERA5's 5 kt is just short). Against the slow flier it works one way only: a wind good to 3.2 kt rules out the balloon if the object really flies near 9.6 kt; nothing rules out the slow flier if it is a balloon. - Pairs no measurement separates. The slow flier and the glare-on-a-target model are the same physics on GOFAST; only a resolved image or the raw recording with known gain could tell them apart. - The size exclusion. Without the D-016 size exclusion the glare-on-a-target model leads instead of the balloon (results above); a resolved, unsaturated image of the object would settle whether that row belongs in the totals.

summary.verdict_text: On the video alone (physics-only), Object on a free path (no physical model) scores highest, ahead of the next explanation by 34.3 log units, but this is not called decisive: with a rotation noise above 12.75 deg (the data-only value is 11.86 deg) H-ART leads instead; in the model-recovery test, data made by H-CLOSE were also won by H-WIT, so this data cannot tell those explanations apart.
summary.settle_title: The radar closure rate at the end of the clip
summary.settle_text: The glare models need the object to hold its distance (about -17 to +12 kt); the free path needs it closing at 48 to 122 kt. A radar closure rate good to about 17 kt would separate them both ways, independent of the rotation noise that decides the leader on the video alone. The ship and E-2 radar tracks the witnesses describe have not been released. - Pairs no measurement separates. The distant jet and the glare-on-a-target model are the same physics here. - The close small object trails by about 1.7 million log units on the real video; the recovery confusion with the free path concerns synthetic data only.
